newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan rejects Kashmir government as puppet.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan rejects Kashmir government as puppet.

text.p: Pakistan on Thursday rejected the installation of a new state administration in the Indian-ruled part of the disputed Kashmir region as a puppet and said the solution lay in a U.N.-mandated plebiscite.

"As could be expected, the Indian authorities have installed a puppet government of (Chief Minister) Farooq Abdullah in (the state summer capital) Srinagar after holding sham state assembly elections in the Indian-held Kashmir," a Foreign Ministry spokesman told reporters.
Abdullah took office on Wednesday after his party last week won the controversial elections, which were boycotted by separatist parties seeking independence or union with Pakistan.
The Pakistani spokesman called about 30 political groups forming the All Parties Hurriyat (Freedom) Conference coalition "the true representatives of the Kashmiri people".
He said the separatist coalition groups had rejected the elections and the new administration's installation, which was marked by protests in the region.
India and Pakistan have fought two of their three wars over the Himalayan region since independence from Britain in 1947.

New Delhi regards the whole region as an integral part of India. But Islamabad wants the predominantly Moslem Kashmiris to exercise their right to self-determination in a U.N.-mandated plebiscite to decide whether to join Islamic Pakistan or predominantly Hindu India.
India accuses Pakistan of arming separatist guerillas who revolted in the region in 1990. Pakistan says it only provides moral and diplomatic support.
Police and hospital sources say more than 20,000 people have been killed in since the insurgency began.
